sentences.text: This creature was a small animal that moved on two legs.
Its anatomy displays a mix of ancient and newer evolutionary features.
The lower leg bone was significantly longer than the upper leg bone, a trait suited for speed.
It possessed eighty-eight teeth in total, including four in the front of the upper jaw and roughly twenty in the upper and lower jaws.
Recent research indicates this species did not have an air sac system inside its bones.
The name combines a word for 'plain' from Quechua and a word for 'runner' from Greek.
The specific name honors the Brazilian paleontologist Mário Costa Barberena.
The genus was first described by Cabreira and colleagues in the year 2011.
Scientists know the animal only from one single specimen, which is a partial but well-preserved skeleton.
The naming team included Sergio F. Cabreira, Cesar L. Schultz, Jonathas S. Bittencourt, Marina B. Soares, Daniel C. Fortier, Lúcio R. Silva, and Max C. Langer.
Cladistic analyses have identified Pampadromaeus as a basal sauropodomorph.
It is classified within the parent group Saturnaliidae.
The species belongs to the family Saturnaliidae.
Pampadromaeus is classified in the class Saurischia.
Pampadromaeus lived during the early Late Triassic, approximately 230 to 228 million years ago.
The time range for Pampadromaeus is the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
Researchers note that the classification of Pampadromaeus as a basal sauropodomorph is not strongly supported due to difficulties in determining its affinities with early dinosaur groups.
